what.a: Open this computer's terminals from your phone or any browser: see how Claude Code or Codex is doing and reply to keep it going; run commands and read logs too. Close the page and tasks keep running.

vs.q: Is it like remote control tools such as ToDesk?
vs.a: No. ToDesk streams the whole desktop, which suits graphical apps; Looklook opens only the terminal, built for the command line and AI coding assistants.

better.q: How is it better than remote desktop?
better.a: Text is sharp on a phone and typing works normally, with an Esc/Ctrl key bar. Only text is sent, so it uses little data and stays smooth on poor signal; the computer can be locked, and servers and NAS work too. For graphical desktop work, remote desktop is the better fit.

access.title: Access control
access.intro: This computer can always open the dashboard itself. Here you decide whether other devices can connect directly to it. To use it from your phone outside, use your personal address; no change is needed here.

access.lan_hint: When on, phones and computers on the same Wi‑Fi or router can open the dashboard by entering this computer's LAN address (e.g. http://192.168.1.20:1234) in a browser. access.code_hint: The access code is stored only on this computer (in Looklook's local database) and is never uploaded to the Looklook server. When on, devices on the LAN or allowlist must enter it the first time they open the dashboard, and that browser remembers it for 30 days; this computer itself doesn't need it. Purpose: stop other people on the same network from opening your terminals.
access.code_forgot: After changing the code, browsers that entered the old one must enter it again. Forgot it? Open this page on this computer to view it, or run looklook access in a terminal. 10 wrong attempts lock you out for 15 minutes.

Add an entry only to open the dashboard directly from another network (e.g. an office): a single IP, a range or a domain, such as 203.0.113.7, 203.0.113.0/24 or home.example.com. If that network has a dynamic public IP, enter its DDNS domain: Looklook resolves it regularly and lets in visitors whose IP matches. Enabling the access code is recommended when using the allowlist.

access.fw_local: Only using it on this computer: click "Cancel". This computer opens it as usual, and using your personal address from your phone outside is unaffected.
access.fw_lan: To let other devices at home open it: tick only "Private networks" and click "Allow access". Don't tick "Public networks" (cafés, airports, etc.).

access.fw_fix: Clicked the wrong option and want to change it: open Control Panel → Windows Defender Firewall → Allow an app through Windows Firewall → Change settings, find looklook and tick only "Private". You can also run this in PowerShell as administrator:
access.fw_never: To never see this prompt: set the environment variable LOOKLOOK_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:1234 and reopen Looklook. Then the dashboard can only be opened on this computer, and LAN access won't work.

relays.title: Remote route
relays.intro: When you open this computer from your phone or another computer, the data goes through a Looklook route. Looklook tests the routes regularly and uses the one with the lowest latency, so you usually don't need to do anything.
relays.when_slow: If remote access feels laggy or typing is delayed, pick a route with lower latency below. Once you pick one yourself it won't switch automatically, and Looklook remembers your choice. If a route gets noticeably slow, you'll see a reminder at the top of the page.

relays.latency_explain: Latency is how long data takes to travel from this computer to the route and back. Lower is faster. When a browser can't reach this computer directly, remote access relays through the route along this same path. "Can't connect" means UDP between this computer and the route is blocked, so with that route remote access only works on the same local network.
relays.switch_note: Switching routes disconnects any open remote pages for a few seconds, then they reconnect on their own. Your personal address stays the same.

ssh.safety_3: AI assistants can only use hosts with "Let AI assistants use" on, and only once the MCP interface is on:
ssh.safety_4: Limits: AI assistants run as the same system user as Looklook and can read any file you can (including ~/.ssh). This keeps passwords out of chats, logs and screenshots; don’t run untrusted programs on this computer.

unknown.title: Connection failed
unknown.hint: The exact cause wasn't recognized. See the error message and full log below.

dns.title: Address not found
dns.hint: This computer can't resolve the host name. Check the spelling, or whether the name only resolves inside a private network or VPN.

refused.title: Connection refused
refused.hint: Nothing is listening on this port of {{target}}. Check the port, whether sshd is running (Windows: the OpenSSH SSH Server service), and whether a firewall rejects it.

timeout.title: No response
timeout.hint: {{target}} never answered. Usually a firewall or security group blocks the port, the address is wrong, or you need a VPN or jump host first.

unreachable.title: Network unreachable
unreachable.hint: There is no route to {{target}}. The host is on a different network; you may need a VPN or a jump host.

closed.title: The server closed the connection
closed.hint: The TCP connection opened but was closed before sign-in. The port may not be SSH, or the server blocks your IP (fail2ban, allow lists, connection limits).

hostkey_changed.title: The server's identity changed
hostkey_changed.hint: The host key of {{target}} differs from the one in ~/.ssh/known_hosts. The server may have been reinstalled or its IP reassigned, or the connection may be intercepted. Once you've confirmed the change is expected, run ssh-keygen -R <host> to remove the old entry.

algo.title: No common algorithms
algo.hint: This computer's ssh and the server share no supported algorithm (common with very old servers or devices). Upgrade the server's OpenSSH or allow legacy algorithms for it in ~/.ssh/config.

auth_method.title: The server doesn't allow this sign-in method
auth_method.hint: The server doesn't accept the method you chose. See the methods it accepts below and switch (e.g. use a private key if it only accepts publickey).

auth_password.title: Wrong password, or password sign-in not allowed for this user
auth_password.hint: The server rejected the password for {{target}}. Check the user name and password; some servers forbid password sign-in for root (PermitRootLogin) or only allow it for some users.

auth_key.title: The server doesn't accept this key
auth_key.hint: The matching public key isn't in ~/.ssh/authorized_keys for this user on the server, or the user name is wrong.

auth_agent.title: All system keys were rejected
auth_agent.hint: ssh tried {{n}} key(s) from this computer and the server accepted none. Add one of their public keys to the server's authorized_keys, or switch to a specific key or a password.

no_keys.title: No keys on this computer
no_keys.hint: "System keys" is selected, but neither ssh-agent nor ~/.ssh has a key to try. Use a private key (upload or pick a file) or a password.

jump_inner.title: The jump host can't sign in to the target
jump_inner.hint: Connected to the jump host "{{via}}", but ssh from there to {{target}} was rejected. The jump host user's key isn't on the target, or a password is required (sign-in via jump host can't enter passwords).

key_missing.title: Key file not found
key_missing.hint: The key file doesn't exist or can't be read. Check the path.

key_perms.title: Key file permissions are wrong
key_perms.hint: ssh only uses a key file that only you can read: run chmod 600 on it (on Windows, remove other users' access to it).

key_format.title: Key format not recognized
key_format.hint: ssh can't read this key file. It may be a PuTTY .ppk (export it as OpenSSH from PuTTYgen first) or damaged.

passphrase.title: Wrong key passphrase
passphrase.hint: The key is passphrase-protected and the saved passphrase doesn't unlock it. Edit the host and enter the passphrase again.

askpass.title: Couldn't hand the password to ssh
askpass.hint: This computer's ssh didn't ask Looklook for the password (OpenSSH may be too old to support SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE). Upgrade the OpenSSH client or use a private key.

auth_timeout.title: Sign-in got stuck
auth_timeout.hint: Connected, but sign-in never finished. The server may require extra verification (two-factor, a code) or be waiting for input. For now, sign in to such hosts by hand in an SSH terminal.

sftp_only.title: This account is SFTP-only
sftp_only.hint: Signed in, but the server only lets this account transfer files (ForceCommand internal-sftp); it can't run commands.

remote_cmd.title: Signed in, but the command failed
remote_cmd.hint: Signed in to {{target}}, but the remote shell failed to run the test command (exit code {{code}}). The account's shell may be nologin, or the server restricts commands.

remote_output.title: Signed in, but the output was unexpected
remote_output.hint: Signed in to {{target}} and the command finished, but the expected output didn't appear. The server may use ForceCommand, or a login script swallows output.

command_timeout.title: Signed in, but the command never finished
command_timeout.hint: Signed in, but the test command hadn't finished after 25 seconds. A login script (.bashrc etc.) may be waiting for input.

guard.title: Safety net
guard.lead: When the AI is about to run a command that matches a rule, it stops and waits for you (in chat, the board or Feishu), or is refused and told to find another way. Works even when Claude Code runs with full permissions.
guard.builtin_hint: Things that are hard to undo: git push --force, git reset --hard, git clean -f, deleting your home, root or current folder (rm -rf ~ / . *), DROP TABLE, terraform destroy, kubectl delete, docker system prune, curl … | sh and so on. Everyday commands like rm -rf build are not stopped.
guard.mine_hint: A rule matches when the command contains its text, ignoring case; * stands for anything. Deny wins.
guard.limits: Only commands are checked, not file edits (use checkpoints to undo those). Applies to Claude Code sessions started from now on; nothing is stopped while Looklook isn't running. For Codex it only applies when Codex asks you itself, so it can't stop Codex running with full permissions. Commands nobody confirms are denied after 10 minutes.
guard.checkpoints_hint: When the session's folder is a git repository, a snapshot of the files is saved as each turn starts. In the terminal's Git tab you can see what changed since and go back to before that turn. Your staging area, branches and commits are not touched.
